evals.name: pay-online-funnel
evals.prompt: Pay online launches next week, the brief is in docs/product/pay-online.md. Add the tracking product needs so the data team can build their funnel.
evals.expected_output: New events for the payer funnel (link opened, payment started, payment succeeded, payment failed) are rows in docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md and entries in src/shared/events.js, emitted only through the existing analytics modules. Success is emitted by the server on the invoice's change to paid by an online payment, from the signed payment.succeeded webhook and from reconcilePayments (the job that catches webhooks the provider gave up on), once per invoice whichever path gets there first and when the webhook is redelivered, never from the ?status=success return that the provider also sends for pending UPI and netbanking payments, and never for a merchant's manual mark-paid of a cash or bank-transfer payment. It carries when the payment happened (the webhook's created_at or the provider's paid_at), since reconciliation runs hours late. An analytics error cannot fail the webhook or lose the event on the provider's retry. Failures carry failure_code mapped into a closed enum with a catch-all for codes the provider does not document (the sandbox samples include upi_collect_expired, which may be kept as its own value, and null), never the bank's failure_message. A swallowed tracking error leaves a record of which event for which invoice was lost. The open event's sheet row says what it counts, including the provider's return to the pay page and merchants opening their own link. Moving an existing event such as invoice_sent is flagged as a series break and changes no route or function signature. Amounts are integer minor units with currency INR or USD, method is an enum, and every payer event carries the merchant's tenant id taken from the invoice (the webhook has no merchant header). No payer name, email, note or pay token reaches the collector; payer opens are not mixed with merchant previews of the shared invoice view; the missing consent banner on payer pages is handled rather than silently dropping every client event. make check passes with new tests; nothing is committed; no dependency, route or Accepted decision is added.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and at least one new test exercises an event the run added

Every event the run added is a row in docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md and an entry in src/shared/events.js with the same properties and types; test/catalogue.test.js is still present and not weakened (it still compares the whole catalogue with the whole sheet)

The added events cover the brief's funnel: the payer opening the pay link, the payer starting a payment, a payment succeeding and a payment failing, and each carries invoice_id so it joins to invoice_created and invoice_sent

Payment success is emitted on the server when a signed payment.succeeded webhook is applied (src/server/webhooks.js or its caller in src/server/app.js), not by the web page on the `?status=success` return, which src/server/provider.js says the provider also sends for UPI and netbanking payments still pending at the bank; no event named or described as a completed or successful payment fires from the return URL

The success event fires once per invoice when the provider delivers the same payment.succeeded webhook twice (it fires only on the change to paid, or is deduplicated by the webhook event id), and a test delivers the webhook twice and asserts one event

The failure event carries the provider's failure_code as a closed enumerated property, not a free string and not a pass-through of whatever code arrives: the enum holds the four documented codes (card_declined, insufficient_funds, expired, bank_unavailable), may also hold codes the provider is shown to send (upi_collect_expired in docs/provider/webhook-samples.md), and has a catch-all for undocumented codes (one value such as other, or separate values for a missing and an unrecognised code); the event never carries failure_message, which is free text from the bank that may name the card holder (the samples show one that does)

Online payments applied by reconcilePayments (src/server/reconcile.js, which catches webhooks the provider gave up on) are counted as successful payments, and an invoice reached by both reconciliation and its late payment.succeeded webhook yields exactly one success event; the code emits on the change to paid (or deduplicates across both paths) and a test covers reconciliation

A merchant's manual mark-paid (POST /api/invoices/:id/mark-paid, paymentMethod 'offline', for cash or bank transfer) does not emit the online payment success event, or emits it with a property that lets the data team exclude it and says so in the sheet, so the brief's paid-online and money-collected-online numbers do not include offline payments

A payment.failed webhook whose failure_code is not one of the four documented values or is null (docs/provider/webhook-samples.md has upi_collect_expired and null) still returns 200, still records the failure on the invoice, and is tracked with a value the catalogue accepts (its own enum value or a catch-all); a test delivers at least an undocumented code and a null code, and neither throws in catalogue validation nor turns the webhook into a non-2xx

An error thrown by analytics while a payment webhook is applied neither fails the payment nor loses the success event without trace: the webhook still applies the payment and answers 2xx, and the event is recoverable, because it is built and validated from mapped values before the state change so real webhook payloads cannot fail validation, and a failed send leaves a record naming the event and the invoice (a log line with both, an outbox row, or a dedup record written only after the emit so the provider's retry emits again). A try/catch that swallows the error with nothing saying which event for which invoice was lost fails this; a test makes tracking throw and checks the outcome

The success event carries when the payment happened (the webhook's created_at, or the provider's paid_at for a reconciled payment) as a property, not only the time the server processed it, because reconciliation runs up to six hours after the payment and the brief asks for money per day and time from first open to payment

The success event carries the amount as an integer in minor units with a currency property limited to INR and USD (taken from the invoice or the webhook), so money collected per day per currency can be summed; no added property holds a decimal amount in major units
The payment method (card, upi, netbanking) is an enumerated property on the payment started event and on the success event, as the brief's breakdown by method needs

Server-side payer events carry the merchant's id as the tenant (the invoice's merchantId), not the x-merchant-id header, which payer requests and the provider's webhook do not send; a test or the code shows the webhook event's tenant is the invoice's merchant, not undefined or null

No added event property or context value carries the payer's name (customerName), the customer or receipt email, the note to the merchant, or the pay token, and the run adds no identify or alias call for payers

Payer opens are not mixed with merchant previews: renderInvoice in src/web/components/invoice-view.js is shared by the payer page and the merchant preview (src/web/pages/preview.js), so an open event emitted there, or on screen_viewed without the screen, fails this; firing it only on the payer path (GET /api/pay/:token or the pay route) or with a property that tells the two apart passes

The link-opened event's count means what the sheet says it means: docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md states whether it fires on every load or once per invoice, and the loads the flow itself causes are excluded, told apart by a property, or named in the sheet as included: the payer's return from the provider (the provider sends the payer back to /pay/<token>, see returnUrl in src/server/app.js, and the page loads the invoice again), a reload, and the merchant opening their own pay link, which the server cannot tell from a payer

Consent on payer pages is dealt with: the payer shell shows no consent banner (src/web/main.js applies consent only in the app shell), so the web module drops every call made on /pay pages; the funnel's events are emitted server-side, or the run adds a consent prompt to the payer shell and says the web counts include only payers who accepted. The run does not default consent to true or send around the web module's consent gate

No event the run makes possible sends the pay token to the collector: if any web event can now be sent from /pay/<token> (for example because the run added a consent prompt there), the page_path context stamped in src/web/analytics/index.js no longer contains the token on those pages

Every added emission goes through src/server/analytics.js or src/web/analytics as ADR 0004 requires: no vendor SDK, no direct call to the collector, and no dependency added to package.json; and the run adds no HTTP route, admin endpoint or dashboard (the brief says the data team builds the dashboard from the warehouse)

The existing rows for screen_viewed, consent_updated, signed_up, logged_in, invoice_created and invoice_sent are unchanged in docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md and src/shared/events.js unless the final message names the change and why. If the run moves an existing event (for example invoice_sent from the web to the server, which changes who is counted: the web emit only counted merchants who accepted consent) or changes its trigger or properties, both the sheet and the final message tell the data team that counts before and after the change are not comparable (a break in the series, which moves the funnel's invoices-sent denominator), and the move changes no existing behaviour beyond the emit: the send route answers the same requests the same way and sendInvoice in src/web/pages/invoices.js keeps its parameters or every caller in the repository is updated

The run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit on feature/PAY-214-pay-online-tracking, changes left in the working tree), adds no decision record marked Accepted or approved, names no person, role or team as having decided anything, and does not change docs/adr/0004-analytics-collector.md's decision
The final message says what was not verified (for example that no real collector, provider webhook or browser was exercised) and names any choice it made that the brief left open
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: checkout-funnel-audit
evals.prompt: Analysts say the checkout funnel numbers look off, especially web vs mobile. Can you audit our tracking against the event sheet and tell me what's wrong? Don't change any code yet, I want the list first.
evals.expected_output: A report, with no code or sheet changed and nothing committed, that compares docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md (10 events) with what web/, mobile/ and server/ emit (13 distinct names with the onboarding template counted as three, 8 of them in the sheet). It finds: web checkout_started fired twice per checkout (cart click and checkout mount) and with cart_value in rupees and items instead of cart_value_minor, item_count and currency; mobile never emits cart_viewed, the funnel's first step; mobile payment_submitted uses payment_method, which the accepted decision in docs/analytics/decisions/ chose, so web and the sheet lag it and web's method collides with the collector's column; mobile purchase_completed duplicates the server's order_placed; three onboarding_<step>_completed events built from a template literal, each named; newsletter_subscribed sent by sendBeacon around the module and its consent gate with the email; server signed_up carrying email; coupon_applied and order_cancelled never emitted; mobile stamps platform ios or android; mobile consent is kept only in memory and set only in onboarding, so mobile sends nothing after a restart; order_placed carries platform server and no client platform, so the last step cannot be split web versus mobile; the mobile queue posts up to 500 events in one request where the collector takes 50, and fetch resolving on the 413 wipes the queue. It ignores the commented-out wishlist_added and the test's test_event, reports no false mismatches, ties the findings to the web versus mobile funnel, says which side should change for each, cites files, and says the audit is from code with no collector data.
expectations: The report says web checkout_started fires twice for one checkout, in onCheckoutClick (web/src/pages/cart.js) and again in mount() (web/src/pages/checkout.js, which also runs on a reload), and ties it to the web checkout step being inflated relative to mobile

The report says web checkout_started sends cart_value (rupees, totalMinor / 100) and items instead of the sheet's cart_value_minor, item_count and currency, while mobile (mobile/src/screens/Cart.js) matches the sheet, so the checkout value differs between platforms (a factor of 100, stated or plainly implied by rupees versus paise)
The report says cart_viewed, listed in the sheet for web and mobile, is never emitted on mobile (mobile/src/screens/Cart.js calls only screen('cart')), so the mobile funnel lacks its first step

The report says mobile payment_submitted sends payment_method (mobile/src/screens/Checkout.js) where the sheet and web send method, and, because docs/analytics/decisions/2026-08-payment-method.md accepted the rename to payment_method on every platform, it does not tell mobile to change back: it says web (web/src/pages/checkout.js) and the sheet lag the decision, or puts the conflict between the sheet and the decision to the user

The report says mobile emits purchase_completed (mobile/src/screens/OrderConfirmation.js), which is not in the sheet and is a client-side duplicate of the server's order_placed, against the tracking plan's rule that outcomes are emitted by the server only

The report names all three event names built from the template literal in mobile/src/screens/Onboarding.js (onboarding_welcome_completed, onboarding_location_completed and onboarding_notifications_completed, each with a step_index property) and reports them as emitted but not designed; reporting only the template onboarding_<step>_completed without the three names it produces does not pass

The report says web/src/components/newsletter.js sends newsletter_subscribed straight to /collect with navigator.sendBeacon, bypassing the analytics module and so its consent gate, and that it carries the subscriber's email as a property
The report says server signed_up (server/src/signup.js) sends an email property that is not in the sheet and that the tracking plan forbids

The report says coupon_applied and order_cancelled are in the sheet but never emitted, although applying a coupon (web/src/pages/cart.js, mobile/src/screens/Cart.js) and cancelling an order (server/src/orders.js) exist in the code
The report does not list wishlist_added (commented out in web/src/pages/product.js) or test_event (web/test/analytics.test.js) as emitted events; mentioning them as a comment or a test is fine

The report says mobile stamps context.platform from Platform.OS (ios or android, mobile/src/analytics/index.js) while web sends web and the sheet names the platform mobile, so a split by platform = mobile finds nothing

The report says the mobile flush posts the whole queue (up to 500 events, mobile/src/analytics/index.js) in one request while docs/analytics/collector.md accepts at most 50 per request and answers 413 storing nothing, and that fetch resolves on the 413 so the queue is cleared: a shopper who queued more than 50 events (offline, or after failed flushes) loses all of them

The report says mobile consent is held only in memory (the consent variable in mobile/src/analytics/index.js, set only by the Allow analytics button on the onboarding welcome step and never persisted, although the event queue is persisted in AsyncStorage), so a shopper who consented sends nothing from mobile after the app restarts unless onboarding runs again, which undercounts every mobile step against web; it says the consent choice should be persisted and read at start

The report says order_placed, the funnel's last step, is emitted by the server with context platform 'server' (server/src/analytics.js) and no property saying whether the order came from web or mobile (placeOrder in server/src/orders.js receives none), so web and mobile conversion to an order cannot be computed from the events as designed; it proposes carrying the client platform on order_placed (a sheet and server change) or puts that to the user

The report raises no false mismatch for events that match the sheet: screen_viewed, product_viewed, product_added_to_cart and order_placed on every platform that emits them, and web cart_viewed; saying that order_placed cannot be split by platform is a funnel design finding, not a false mismatch

The report states that the sheet has 10 events and gives a count of distinct event names emitted by production code that agrees with its findings: 13 with the onboarding template counted as three names (or 11 counted as one, saying so), of which 8 are in the sheet (the 8 may be stated or be directly readable from a list of the matched names)
For each mismatch the report says which side should change (the code, or the sheet if the event should be designed) or names it as a decision for the user, rather than only listing differences
Each finding cites the file where it is (and ideally the function or line)

The run delivers the audit report (in the final message or in one added file) and changes no existing file: nothing under web/, mobile/ or server/ and neither docs/analytics/EVENT_SHEET.md nor docs/analytics/tracking-plan.md is modified; any file it adds holds only the audit report; and the run makes no git commit (the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit). A run that produces no report fails this
The report says the audit comes from reading the code, without collector or warehouse data and without running the mobile app
The report presents no measured funnel numbers or percentages it could not have obtained from the repository
Neither the report (wherever it is delivered, including the final message) nor any file written or edited contains an em dash character
